text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- President Jacques Chirac wades into French parliamentary race, calling for for a new, shared sense of initiative and solidarity to meet future challenges
-- Court sentences former Alcatel Alsthom chairman Pierre Suard to a three-year suspended prison term for plundering company funds to pay for security work on his private homes
-- Auchan family-owned supermarkets group concludes long-term alliance with Italian supermarket chain La Rinascente, controlled by the Agnelli family.
-- Insurer AGF considers bidding for GAN.
-- Socialist party calls for state controls on firms' right to lay off staff, while the conservative coalition calls for labour market flexibility.
-- Fund managers puzzled by polls on voters' intentions for upcoming parliamentary election.
-- Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere to file offers today for the state's 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF defence electronics group.
-- Managing board at Eramet threaten to resign with chairman Yves Rambaud in a crisis with majority shareholder Erap over New Caledonian nickel mining fields.
